neighborhoods.name: Gangnam (Teheran-ro / Yeoksam corridor)
neighborhoods.rationale: AI Tinkerers Seoul held its inaugural demo night here (Jul 2025), both Cursor Seoul Meetups 2025 ran at Hashed Lounge (K-Square Gangnam, Jun) and Dangun Software Seocho (Oct), AWS HQ Yeoksam hosted Day 1 of the Students@AI Seoul Hackathon (Apr 2025), and AMD/Moreh ran an AI Dev Meetup at Aloft Gangnam (Dec 2025) - the densest Teheran-ro cluster of bilingual AI/builder events, with Centerfield, Maru180, D.CAMP, Hashed Lounge, and K-Square offering 100-200p event-capable floors.

avoid_too: Tour-only hanok cafes (Cafe Onion main room) - no reservation policy and constant foot traffic
Seoul Forest pop-up strip - short-lease brand pop-ups, not stable event venues
Cafe-lined Seoul Forest west edge - tiny 20-40p specialty cafes that will not buy out
neighborhoods.name: Seongsu-dong (Seoul Forest east edge)
neighborhoods.rationale: Seongsu is where Seoul's warehouse-conversion cafes double as hack venues: Elice Lab at 280 Seongsu-dong 2-ga ran Day 1 of the Students@AI Seoul Hackathon (Apr 12-13 2025, 100+ builders, AWS/Upstage/Perplexity-backed), Seoul Startup Hub Seongsu runs recurring startup/AI/ESG programs (Lotte Construction x Seongsu Open Innovation 2026), and large-footprint venues (Daelim Changgo, Seongsu Yeonbang, Elice Lab itself) genuinely support 50-200p semi-private bookings - the only Seoul neighborhood where a 'coffee + hack day' format is the default, not an exception.

avoid_too: Hongdae club strip (south of station) - nightlife, no daytime bookable event cafes
Yonsei campus halls (Baekyang/New Millennium) - university booking only, not open to external commercial events
Hongdae fashion-week runway venues - event-priced, no drop-in cowork character
neighborhoods.name: Sinchon / Hongdae (Mapo-Seodaemun university belt)
neighborhoods.rationale: Yonsei Sinchon campus hosted the 2025 Asia Impact Hackathon (May) and GDG on Campus Yonsei ran the Korea x Japan SW-AI Hackathon 'The Bridge' (May 2025), SKYST consortium (SNU/Yonsei/Korea/KAIST) rotates 100-150 person hackathons here, Dev Korea holds bilingual English-first meetups in the area, and Founders Running Club Seoul lists Hongdae as a recurring host - the strongest bilingual KR/EN student-and-indie-builder density, anchored by Yonsei/Ewha/Hongik and Mapo's indie event spaces (D.Camp spinoffs, Live House Hongdae, extensible cafes).
